title: Evaluating and Improving Value Judgments in AI: A Scenario-Based Study on Large Language Models' Depiction of Social Conventions

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting the model with fill-in-the-blank queries about the social perception of highly educated women (Ph.D. holders) as marriage partners and women's safety walking at night across various countries, then comparing the sentiment of the responses to official indices like OECD data and the Women Peace and Security Index.

Prompting the model with fill-in-the-blank queries about how people with disabilities feel towards their government across different countries, and comparing the positivity of the model's responses with OECD data on social spending.

Prompting the model with fill-in-the-blank queries regarding how LGBTQ+ individuals feel within different countries' societies, and correlating the responses with the Social Acceptance of LGBTI People index.
Prompting the model with fill-in-the-blank queries about societies' attitudes toward immigrants across various countries, and comparing the results to OECD data on permanent immigrant inflows.

Presenting the model with a prompt about a recent controversy (the censorship of Michelle Yeoh's Oscar speech) in five different languages (English, French, Korean, Japanese, and Chinese) and qualitatively analyzing the differences in tone and cultural perspective across the responses.
